messages:
Maya Liang: Thinking out loud — proposing a new 'surge-snapback' mode for staged rollouts when a region hits transient overload. Goal: let a feature ramp in but automatically snap back to a safer config if latency/capacity signals exceed thresholds.

Tom H.: +1 need this. Can you sketch high-level phases and flag semantics?

Maya Liang: Sure. Phases: warmup (low sample), expansion (higher sample), snapback (auto-decrease + partial traffic shed). Flag semantics: opt-in per-tenant, global admin override, per-region sampler.

Jordan P.: Important to define which fallbacks we do in snapback — do we route to next-best region, downgrade model size, or queue? We should prioritize lowest user-visible impact.

Maya Liang: Priority order I propose: 1) route to healthy region (if geo-tolerant), 2) switch to quantized/cheaper model variant, 3) enable degraded response (shorter completion) or queue.

Sara V.: For geo routing, need consent/opt-in for latency-sensitive customers. Also legal/reg compliance flags for region failover. Add per-tenant geofence option.

Tom H.: Good call. What metrics drive snapback? 95th p95 latency > X, provisioned GPU usage > Y%, error rate spike > Z, and sudden drop in available KV cache hit rate.

Maya Liang: Exactly. We'll expose these as threshold config:
```
flag: surge_snapback
phases:
  - warmup: sample 1-5% for 10m
  - expansion: sample to target % over 30m
  - snapback: auto-decrease to 0 or fallback variant on thresholds
metrics_thresholds:
  p95_latency_ms: 1200
  gpu_util_pct: 92
  error_rate_pct: 1.5
```

Kevin R.: Ops questions: who owns the kill-switch? We should have an automated snapback plus a manual global kill (and regional) that the oncall can hit. ops-bot should post a remediation checklist.

ops-bot: noted — will create a runbook stub if we add the flag. Suggest adding Slack alert on rule triggers + automatic incident with prefilled fields.

Jordan P.: For A/B testing compatibility — can we run deterministic buckets so experiments don't get biased by snapbacks? Need to mark experiments as sticky to user cohort and decouple experiment buckets from routing fallback decisions.

Maya Liang: Plan: experiment assignment is stable; routing fallback can affect delivered variant but we surface that in telemetry and mark impacted requests. Add a header: X-snapback-reason.

Sara V.: Telemetry: we need per-tenant exploded metrics (latency, cost delta, fallback rate) and a daily report for customers in opt-in. Also add an SLA impact estimator in console before enabling.

Tom H.: Rollout plan: 1) internal dogfood (10% infra traffic) for 48h, 2) partner opt-ins (select customers) at 1-5% for 7d, 3) broader GA opt-in with 24/7 oncall, 4) auto-enable for some non-latency-critical tenants.

Maya Liang: Canary gating checklist: warmup health OK (no p95 spikes), KV hit rate stable, no model OOMs, ops runbook validated. If any failure, immediate rollback to pre-flag routing.

Kevin R.: Add cost-guard too — if cost per 1M tokens increases > 15% inside the experiment window, auto-snapback.

Jordan P.: Conflicts to surface: Dedicated customers with reserved capacity may not accept region routing fallback. Need explicit denylist and a per-tenant policy UI.

Maya Liang: Action items:
- Maya: write PR for flag schema + default thresholds (this week)
- Tom: add alert rules and ops-bot runbook entries (this week)
- Kevin: add cost guard hook to optimizer pipeline (next sprint)
- Jordan: design experiment stickiness + X-snapback-reason header (next sprint)
- Sara: telemetry dashboard mock + SLA estimator copy (this sprint)

Tom H.: Happy path testcases? Add load-jerk test, sudden-region-blackhole sim, and model-variant-fallback test.

Maya Liang: Great. If no objections, I'll file the RFC and schedule a 30-min sync to walk through the thresholds and the console UI. :thumbsup:

Sara V.: Sounds good to me. +1 for tenant denylist.

Kevin R.: +1. Ops ready for runbook.

Jordan P.: +1. Will mock telemetry events.

ops-bot: RFC issue created: infra/rfcs#1248 (auto). Runbook stub: /runbooks/surge_snapback (draft).
